title: Michael Carrick encouraged by meeting with Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe
content:
Michael Carrick met with Sir Jim Ratcliffe during the Manchester United co-owner’s visit to Carrington last week, as club executives continue to weigh up who to appoint as their next permanent manager.

Ratcliffe was at United’s training base on Monday, April 20, a week after attending Old Trafford to watch the team’s defeat to Leeds United. But 48 hours prior to Ratcliffe’s return to Manchester, Carrick’s side beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge to move within touching distance of Champions League qualification.

That background provided a happy setting for Ratcliffe’s conversation with interim boss Carrick, who is among the contenders to be appointed as United head coach once the campaign is finished.

“He came in, we had a chat, we had a cup of tea,” said Carrick. “A casual chat to be honest, it was nice to see him showing his support, obviously. That was it. It was quite informal, but it was nice to see him.”

Ratcliffe was able to get a sense of how Carrick operates at Carrington from visiting the complex and his view on what direction United go in this summer will be important.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are leading the process, and plan to make the recommendation only at the end of the season, but background checks on candidates are being carried out now.

Carrick welcomed Ratcliffe’s effort to get a firsthand view of daily life at United.

“I think as a football club we’re hugely connected all the way through,” he said. “I think it’s a big part and I’m really conscious of that’s how it should be, and I am trying to do my part with that, as well as is everybody else. So, I’ve felt that since I’ve been here since January for sure.”

Carrick said he has a good understanding with his coaching team about their own futures amid the current uncertainty beyond May. He brought in Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate and Jonny Evans to work with him when being appointed on an interim basis in January. Travis Binnion was promoted from the academy.

“We’re very close,” Carrick said. “Even though we came together specifically for the role here, we’re all very clear in terms of what it looks like. It’s not something that we need to overly discuss, to be honest. I think we’re all on the same page. We know it. We’re right and the coaches are fine with that.

He added: “Sometimes you connect with people and you work well. For me, it is all about people, whether that’s players or staff or supporters, family, whatever it is. I think connecting with people is really important to try and get the best out of each other.

“I have to say the staff have been absolutely top-class in different ways, different personalities, different roles. To come together in a coaching office that’s not much bigger than this desk, to be around the desk day in day out when it’s new and it’s fresh takes a lot of effort, but credit to everyone it’s been all positive.”

Ratcliffe meeting Carrick at this point in the season is significant, even if just to chew the fat over a brew. Carrick might not possess the heart-on-sleeve press conference personality that people who have worked with Ratcliffe believe he goes for, but the 44-year-old does have a quiet steel and sharp mind, which would come to the fore during a one-on-one conversation.

United have taken 26 points from 12 games since Carrick took charge at United – only Pep Guardiola has taken more with Manchester City in that period. But those in charge want to wait until the end of the campaign to make their decision, when all the data can be factored in. In the meantime Carrick is showing what he can do now, and he has support from players. Getting a sense of that could be telling for Ratcliffe.

Additionally, the fact that so many of the managers considered contenders have the World Cup to deal with first is a major complication for United. Thomas Tuchel, Julian Nagelsmann and Carlo Ancelotti would hope to still be leading England, Germany and Brazil, respectively, at a stage when United’s pre-season gets under way.

Carrick, by contrast, could start preparation for 2026-27 as soon as the final whistle blows on United’s last game of the season at Brighton & Hove Albion.
